info.title: CeleOne API
info.description:
API reference for the current CeleOne Laravel backend.

Base URL: https://api.celeonetv.com/api. Authenticate using a returned access_token in the Authorize dialog. Dates use ISO 8601 unless a field explicitly describes milliseconds. Scheduled posts are published by the backend scheduler. Profile privacy is enforced for other viewers; owners retain access to their own contact details.

Dynamic resource payloads are JSON objects whose fields depend on the collection or domain. GET/HEAD share the same behavior; PUT and PATCH aliases are both listed. Internal callbacks require service keys. The legacy signed content upload route is marked unavailable because its handler is absent. Try it out sends real requests to the live API.

Also includes the notification, call configuration, and payment HTTP endpoints routed by api.celeonetv.com. Companion service contracts were checked against their running source.

post.description:
Requires a Sanctum bearer token from login, Google sign-in, or Firebase token exchange.

Rate limit: 5,1 (requests, minutes).

IMPORTANT:
This endpoint intentionally remains compatible with old
Cèlè One mobile builds.

Old application flow:

Google
  -> Firebase signInWithCredential()
  -> Firebase user.getIdToken()
  -> POST /api/v1/auth/firebase/exchange
  -> Laravel Sanctum token

No mobile rebuild is required for this flow.

get.summary: Owner-only lifetime statistics over all page publications, not a feed sample. Reach is summed per-content unique viewers

totalViews.description: Recorded viewing sessions plus preserved historical counts. Retries are deduplicated; new owner/manager views are excluded.

reach.description: Sum of unique authenticated viewers per content item. A person viewing two items contributes two.

uniqueAudience.description: Distinct authenticated viewers across the entire page, counted once.

legacyViews.description: Historical aggregate view baseline retained at migration. Historical reach requires identifiable viewer records.

examples: Only page managers can see analytics.
